introduction: On this Sunday, Moses gives Israel the great prayer: Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord alone; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart. In the Gospel, a scribe asks Jesus which commandment is the first, and Jesus joins love of God with love of neighbor. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Jesus lives forever to intercede for us. Let us love God and our neighbor with all our heart.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our rock and our strength. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may teach by her life that love of God and love of neighbor cannot be separated. Let us pray to the Lord.
For parents: that they may pass on the faith to their children by word and example. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our neighbors in need, near and far: that we may love them as we love ourselves. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are seeking God sincerely: that they may come close to his Kingdom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may love God with all our heart, soul, mind and strength. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you are one, and you command us to love you above all and our neighbor as ourselves. Pour your love into our hearts, so that we may keep your commandments. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The first of all commandments
reflection.body:
Every day, faithful Jews pray the words of today's first reading, the Shema: "Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God. The LORD is one. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might." Moses wants these words to be kept close: "These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart." They are to be taught to children and grandchildren.

In the Gospel, a scribe asks Jesus a question the rabbis often discussed: "Which commandment is the greatest of all?" Jesus answers with the Shema, and then adds a second commandment from the Law: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself." And he concludes, "There is no other commandment greater than these." Jesus does not separate the two. Love of God shows itself in love of neighbor, and love of neighbor is rooted in love of God.

The scribe agrees warmly and says that this love is "more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices." Jesus sees that he has understood and tells him, "You are not far from God's Kingdom."

The psalm gives us words to express this love: "I love you, LORD, my strength." Love of God is not only a duty; it is the answer of a heart that has been loved and saved.

The Letter to the Hebrews reminds us that Jesus himself helps us to love. He is a priest who "lives forever to make intercession for them."

This week, pray the words of the Shema each morning, slowly, as an offering of your whole self to God. Then look for one neighbor who needs your love today, and love them as you would want to be loved.
